text:
Edmonton had this one finished before the first intermission was over. Four goals in the opening 20 minutes, the last of them Ryan Shea's with 28 seconds left, put EDM up 4-0, and Leon Draisaitl made it 5-0 just 27 seconds into the second. The chance quality backed it up: EDM generated 1.53 expected goals in the first period to Vancouver's 0.14. Connor McDavid, who finished with a goal and four assists, even added a shorthanded goal, and Kasperi Kapanen followed with another 34 seconds later to make it 8-2.

Then the game turned strange. Vancouver outchanced Edmonton 1.84 to 0.53 in the third, and Marco Rossi scored twice in under three minutes to cut it to 8-5. Elias Pettersson's power-play slap shot made it 8-6, and Draisaitl's own power-play goal restored the cushion at 9-6. Jamie Oleksiak scored late for 9-7, but it was too little. Rossi finished with two goals and an assist in just over 15 minutes of ice time.

Goaltending shaped the scoreline more than the shot quality did. Kevin Lankinen allowed eight goals on roughly 2.3 expected, a cost of nearly six goals, while Devon Levi gave up seven against about 2.9 expected. At even strength Vancouver held the edge in chance quality, 2.45 to 1.89, and EDM's 57 percent deserved-to-win figure is far thinner than the five-goal lead suggested. Edmonton took the early game, Vancouver took the late one, and the early one was worth far more.
